page: monitor/ pipeline infrastructure (not a dome-site change)
description: FOLLOW-UP on chg-20260808-1620-001 (6-day pipeline write/push stall, critical/HIGH). Since last poll, tinker ran a Mode 2 outage diagnosis (commit 1385246, 2026-08-08T18:15Z local) that root-caused the stall to the HOST-level /sessions device being 100% full (distinct from the /tmp partition this poller and other clone-based agents use), which blocked all ${SESSION}-prefixed clone paths for 6 days. Tinker rescued 12 stranded FUSE artifacts (WIN-021.c6 + WIN-002.c5 reviews, ISS-3043 analyst work, tracker/attention-inbox/status merges) and authored + applied PROP-148 (commit b7fc9ce): clone-target /tmp fallback + fail-closed disk gates + sessions_fs_avail_mb telemetry, so future agent clones default to /tmp instead of the exhausted /sessions mount. This poller's own clone (at /tmp/poller-clone) completed without issue, consistent with the fix. HOWEVER: /sessions is STILL reported 100% full (0 bytes available) as of this poll -- PROP-148 works around the symptom for clone-based agents but does not resolve the underlying host-level disk exhaustion. Only 2 commits landed in the review repo since the last poll (integrity's 08-08T15:25 WARN report and tinker's 08-08T18:15 fix) -- no decider/curmudgeon/analyst work has resumed yet, so the multi-day triage backlog (WIN-021/WIN-047/WIN-055 attention-inbox items, curmudgeon queue) is likely still unprocessed pending the next scheduled runs of those agents.
before: chg-20260808-1620-001: 6-day, 8-of-9-agent stall observed; root cause suspected disk pressure; /sessions and /tmp both under pressure at that time.
after: Root cause confirmed (host-level /sessions 100% full) and workaround shipped (PROP-148, clone-target /tmp fallback). /sessions remains 100% full at this poll's check. No decider/curmudgeon/analyst commits yet since the fix landed -- next scheduled runs of those agents should be checked for resumption.
suggested_fix: Next poll should confirm decider/curmudgeon/analyst have resumed committing (i.e. PROP-148 actually restores full pipeline function, not just poller/tinker/integrity). /sessions host-level exhaustion itself may need operator-level intervention (it's outside git-repo scope) if it isn't self-clearing -- flag to tinker/operator if it's still 100% full after 2-3 more polls.
